name: GTSIGN-220
description: Robust traffic sign recognition is critical for autonomous driving, intelligent transportation systems, and smart city applications. Multiple datasets for German roads exist, but often fail to capture the full complexity of real-world conditions and regulations. They often lack sufficient class diversity, especially concerning the many additional signs that provide essential contextual information. Synthetic datasets, while scalable, do not fully incorporate all real-world visual effects. To bridge this gap, we present the German Traffic SIGNs (GTSIGN-220) dataset, a new, large-scale benchmark of over 75,000 real-world images across 220 classes. As a key contribution, our dataset was gathered through a nationwide crowdsourcing effort in Germany, ensuring high diversity in camera types, viewpoints, weather conditions, and lighting conditions. It authentically represents in-the-wild challenges such as partial occlusion, motion blur, and vandalism. The inclusion of numerous additional signs enables advanced driver-assistance systems to process nuanced information, such as road damage warnings or specific exemptions. Critically, the dataset’s alignment with the official German Traffic Regulations (StVO) makes it directly applicable for local administrations to automate the inventory and maintenance of their sign databases, bridging the gap between research and practical municipal needs.
